content: Healthcare organizations, such as the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), provide evidence-based guidance to assist healthcare systems in improving diabetes care practices. By leveraging tools like patient registries, healthcare providers can systematically collect and organize patient data to monitor and enhance care delivery. Additionally, the use of electronic health records (EHRs) enables health systems to assess the quality of care provided, track patient outcomes over time, and implement structured quality improvement cycles to address gaps in care and optimize clinical outcomes.
